text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Royal Canadian Mounted Police tactics warlike, trial told: Hollow-point bullets used in British Columbia native standoff, Mountie testifies.
- Canadian Labour Congress president suggested Ontario default: Former premier Bob Rae's memoirs cite fight with Bob White.
- Go slow, Lebed urges NATO: Weigh expansion in Europe, he says.
- Heritage Minister Sheila Copps moves to save Banff National Park from extinction: Airstrip closing, demolitions ordered after crisis report. - Doctors cautious on spanking
ban: Pediatric group's guidelines avoid calling for law against corporal punishment.
- Trade entangles fund star: Veronika Hirsch criticized by ex-boss at AGF Management Ltd for not reporting investment in firm made ahead of fund.
- Rolls-Royce to shed Bristol: Struggling aerospace firm no longer fits plans but Bombardier shows interest.
- Impact of General Motors of Canada strike hits U.S.: 1,850 laid off at supplier plants.
- Radio trade spat brewing: U.S. warns Canada about pay audio.
- Dow Jones flirts with 6,000 level: Stock index loses gain, expected to close above mark soon.

- Banks put hope in hybrid Guaranteed Investment Certificates: Billions of dollars in GICs are coming up for renewal at a time when interest rates are at their lowest levels in years. The banks are trying to make them more attractive.
- Rolls-Royce hangs for-sale sign on Winnipeg's Bristol Aerospace.
